questions.text: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable whose value can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: let creates a block-scoped binding that can be reassigned. const is also block-scoped, but its binding cannot be reassigned.

questions.text: Which keyword declares a variable binding that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the binding. It does not make an object stored in that binding immutable.

questions.text: JavaScript is case-sensitive, so userName and username can refer to different variables.
questions.explanation: JavaScript identifiers are case-sensitive. userName and username are different names.

questions.text: Which value represents the intentional absence of an object value?
questions.explanation: null is commonly used to represent an intentional absence of a value. undefined usually means a value has not been assigned.

questions.text: What is the result of typeof 42?
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses the number type for ordinary numeric values, so typeof 42 returns "number".

questions.text: Which operator checks both value and type equality without coercion?
questions.explanation: === performs strict equality without type coercion. == may coerce values before comparing them.

questions.text: Which syntax creates a single-line comment?
questions.explanation: // starts a single-line JavaScript comment. /* ... */ is used for block comments.

questions.text: Which syntax creates an array with three numbers?
questions.explanation: Array literals use square brackets, so [1, 2, 3] creates an array containing three numbers.

questions.text: Array indexes in JavaScript start at 0.
questions.explanation: The first array element is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on.

questions.text: Which property gives the number of elements in an array?
questions.explanation: The length property reports an array's length. Arrays do not have built-in size or count properties.

questions.text: Which method adds an item to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push() appends one or more items to an array and returns the new length.

questions.text: Which method removes and returns the last item of an array?
questions.explanation: pop() removes and returns the final array element. shift() does the same at the beginning.

questions.text: Which keyword begins a basic conditional statement?
questions.explanation: if starts a conditional branch that runs when its condition is truthy.

questions.text: Which operator means logical AND?
questions.explanation: && is the logical AND operator. It evaluates to the first falsy operand, or the last operand if all are truthy.

questions.text: Which operator means logical NOT?
questions.explanation: ! negates the truthiness of a value. For example, !true evaluates to false.

questions.text: The string "5" and the number 5 are strictly equal with ===.
questions.explanation: === does not coerce types. A string and a number are not strictly equal even when their displayed values look the same.

questions.text: Which syntax creates a string value?
questions.explanation: JavaScript strings can use double quotes, single quotes, or backticks. Backticks create a template literal, which is still a string value.

questions.text: Which operator joins strings together in a basic expression?
questions.explanation: The + operator concatenates strings when at least one operand is a string.

questions.text: Which expression converts the string "42" to a number?
questions.explanation: Number("42") converts the numeric string to the number 42.

questions.text: What does console.log() primarily do in a browser?
questions.explanation: console.log() writes a value or message to the browser's developer console, which is useful for debugging.

questions.text: Which statement immediately exits a loop?
questions.explanation: break exits the nearest loop or switch statement. continue skips to the next loop iteration instead.

questions.text: Which statement skips the rest of the current loop iteration?
questions.explanation: continue ends the current iteration and proceeds with the next loop check.

questions.text: A function can return a value with the return statement.
questions.explanation: return ends the current function call and can provide a value back to the caller.

questions.text: Which is a valid function declaration?
questions.explanation: A function declaration uses the function keyword followed by a name, parentheses, and a body.

questions.text: What are the names inside a function definition's parentheses called?
questions.explanation: Parameters are names declared by the function. Arguments are the actual values supplied when the function is called.

questions.text: Which syntax calls a function named greet?
questions.explanation: Parentheses invoke a function, so greet() calls the function named greet.

questions.text: Which loop is commonly used when you know the number of iterations?
questions.explanation: A for loop is commonly used when initialization, condition, and update logic fit naturally together.

questions.text: Which comparison operator means greater than or equal to?
questions.explanation: >= tests whether the left operand is greater than or equal to the right operand.

questions.text: Which operator returns the remainder after division?
questions.explanation: % is the remainder operator. For example, 7 % 3 evaluates to 1.

questions.text: NaN stands for a special numeric value meaning Not-a-Number.
questions.explanation: NaN is a special number value used for invalid numeric results, even though typeof NaN is "number".

questions.text: Which syntax creates an object with a name property?
questions.explanation: Object literals use curly braces with key-value pairs, such as {name: "Ada"}.

questions.text: How can you read the name property from an object called user?
questions.explanation: Dot notation reads a property by name, so user.name accesses the name property.

questions.text: Which value is falsy?
questions.explanation: The number 0 is falsy. The non-empty string "0", arrays, and objects are truthy.

questions.text: Which value is a boolean?
questions.explanation: true and false are the two boolean values in JavaScript. "true" is a string.

questions.text: An empty string "" is falsy in JavaScript.
questions.explanation: The empty string is one of JavaScript's falsy values.

questions.text: Which expression increases x by 1?
questions.explanation: x += 1 adds 1 to x and assigns the result back to x. x++ would also increment by 1.

questions.text: Which expression creates a template literal?
questions.explanation: Template literals use backticks and can interpolate expressions with ${...}.

questions.text: Which keyword provides an alternative branch after if?
questions.explanation: else runs when the preceding if condition is not truthy.

questions.text: Which statement is useful for comparing one expression against several case values?
questions.explanation: switch compares one expression with case labels and can be clearer than a long chain of equality checks.

questions.text: Which loop keeps running while its condition remains truthy?
questions.explanation: A while loop repeats as long as its condition evaluates to a truthy value.

questions.text: Which expression reads the first character of a string named text?
questions.explanation: Strings support indexed access, so text[0] reads the first character.

questions.text: const means the value stored inside an object can never change.
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the binding. Properties of a const object can still be changed unless the object is otherwise restricted.

questions.text: Which array method removes the first element and returns it?
questions.explanation: shift() removes and returns the first array element. unshift() adds items to the beginning.

questions.text: Which array method adds an item to the beginning?
questions.explanation: unshift() inserts one or more items at the start of an array and returns the new length.

questions.text: What does typeof "hello" return?
questions.explanation: typeof returns "string" for string primitive values.

questions.text: Which keyword declares a variable using older function-scoped syntax?
questions.explanation: var is the older variable declaration form. Unlike let and const, it is function-scoped rather than block-scoped.

questions.text: The expression 2 ** 3 evaluates to 8.
questions.explanation: ** is the exponentiation operator, so 2 ** 3 means 2 to the power of 3.

questions.text: Which expression tests whether x is less than 10?
questions.explanation: The < operator tests whether the left operand is less than the right operand.

questions.text: Which built-in function parses an integer from the start of a string?
questions.explanation: parseInt() parses an integer from the beginning of a string, stopping when parsing can no longer continue.

questions.text: Which Math method rounds a number down to the nearest integer?
questions.explanation: Math.floor() returns the greatest integer less than or equal to the input. For negative values, this differs from truncation.

questions.text: What is the scope of a variable declared with let inside a block?
questions.explanation: let is block-scoped, so the binding exists only within the surrounding block and nested blocks.

questions.text: What does Array.prototype.map() return?
questions.explanation: map() calls a function for each element and returns a new array containing the returned values.

questions.text: Array.prototype.filter() returns a new array and does not remove items from the original array by itself.
questions.explanation: filter() creates a new array containing elements whose callback result is truthy. It does not mutate the source array by itself.

questions.text: Which array method returns the first element whose callback is truthy?
questions.explanation: find() returns the first matching element, or undefined if no element matches.

questions.text: Which array method checks whether at least one element passes a test?
questions.explanation: some() returns true if at least one element makes the callback truthy.

questions.text: Which array method checks whether every element passes a test?
questions.explanation: every() returns true only if the callback is truthy for every element, with the usual empty-array behavior of true.

questions.text: What does destructuring allow you to do?
questions.explanation: Destructuring syntax extracts values from arrays or properties from objects into variables or parameters.

questions.text: Object destructuring can assign a property to a variable with a different name.
questions.explanation: Object destructuring supports renaming, such as const {name: userName} = user.

questions.text: What does ...items mean in a function parameter list?
questions.explanation: In a parameter list, ...items is a rest parameter that collects remaining arguments into an array.

questions.text: What does ...arr do inside an array literal?
questions.explanation: Spread syntax expands iterable values into the surrounding array literal.

questions.text: Which operator provides a fallback only when the left side is null or undefined?
questions.explanation: ?? is the nullish coalescing operator. Unlike ||, it does not replace other falsy values such as 0 or "".

questions.text: What does user?.profile do when user is null?
questions.explanation: Optional chaining short-circuits and returns undefined when the value before ?. is null or undefined.

questions.text: Which syntax exports a named binding from an ES module?
questions.explanation: The export keyword exposes a named binding from an ES module.

questions.text: ES module import declarations are only allowed in module code, not ordinary classic scripts.
questions.explanation: Static import declarations are part of ES module syntax. Classic scripts cannot contain them.

questions.text: Which syntax imports a named export called sum?
questions.explanation: Named exports are imported with braces, such as import { sum } from "./math.js".

questions.text: Which method selects the first DOM element matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector() returns the first element matching the given CSS selector, or null if none matches.

questions.text: Which method returns a static NodeList of all DOM elements matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelectorAll() returns a static NodeList containing all matching elements.

questions.text: Which method adds an event listener without replacing existing listeners of the same type?
questions.explanation: addEventListener() registers a listener and can coexist with other listeners for the same event type.

questions.text: event.preventDefault() always stops the event from bubbling.
questions.explanation: preventDefault() cancels the event's default action when cancelable. stopPropagation() is used to stop propagation.

questions.text: Which method stops an event from continuing through the propagation path?
questions.explanation: stopPropagation() prevents further capture and bubbling through ancestors, but it does not cancel the default action.

questions.text: What is a closure?

answers.text: A function plus access to outer scope

questions.explanation: A closure is a function together with access to the lexical environment where it was created.

questions.text: Which statement about arrow functions is correct?
questions.explanation: Arrow functions do not bind their own this; they use this from the surrounding lexical scope.

questions.text: What does JSON.stringify() usually produce from a JavaScript value?
questions.explanation: JSON.stringify() serializes supported JavaScript values into JSON text.

questions.text: What does JSON.parse() do?

answers.text: Parses JSON text into a value

questions.explanation: JSON.parse() converts valid JSON text into the corresponding JavaScript value.

questions.text: JSON.stringify() preserves functions as executable functions in the resulting JSON.
questions.explanation: JSON has no function type. Function-valued object properties are omitted, and functions in arrays become null.

questions.text: Which keyword marks a function so that it always returns a Promise?
questions.explanation: An async function always returns a Promise, wrapping a non-Promise return value when needed.

questions.text: Where can await normally be used in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: await is valid inside async functions, and top-level await is also valid in ES modules.

questions.text: What does await do to a fulfilled Promise?
questions.explanation: await pauses that async evaluation until settlement and produces the fulfillment value, without blocking the JavaScript thread.

questions.text: Which Promise method registers fulfillment and rejection handlers?
questions.explanation: then() registers handlers and returns a new Promise.

questions.text: Which Promise method is commonly used to handle a rejection?
questions.explanation: catch() registers a rejection handler and returns a new Promise.

questions.text: Promise.prototype.finally() receives the fulfillment value as its first argument.
questions.explanation: finally() is called without the Promise's fulfillment value or rejection reason. It is intended for cleanup logic.

questions.text: Which syntax gives a default parameter value of 10?
questions.explanation: Default parameters use = in the parameter list. The default is used when the argument is missing or explicitly undefined.

questions.text: What does arr.includes(value) return?
questions.explanation: includes() returns true if the array contains the searched value and false otherwise.

questions.text: Which string method tests whether a string begins with a given substring?
questions.explanation: startsWith() returns a boolean indicating whether the string begins with the supplied substring.

questions.text: Which syntax is an object method shorthand?
questions.explanation: Inside an object literal, greet() {} is shorthand method syntax.

questions.text: A variable declared with const must be initialized when it is declared.
questions.explanation: A const declaration requires an initializer because the binding cannot later be assigned for the first time.

questions.text: What does Object.keys(obj) return?
questions.explanation: Object.keys() returns an array of the object's own enumerable string-keyed property names.

questions.text: What does Object.values(obj) return?
questions.explanation: Object.values() returns the values of the object's own enumerable string-keyed properties.

questions.text: What does Object.entries(obj) return?
questions.explanation: Object.entries() returns an array of [key, value] pairs for own enumerable string-keyed properties.

questions.text: Which loop directly iterates values from an iterable such as an array?
questions.explanation: for...of iterates values from an iterable. for...in iterates enumerable string property names.

questions.text: for...in is generally intended to iterate enumerable property names rather than array values.
questions.explanation: for...in visits enumerable string property names, including inherited ones unless filtered. for...of is usually better for array values.

questions.text: Which method copies an array shallowly without changing it?
questions.explanation: slice() with no arguments returns a shallow copy. splice() mutates the original array.

questions.text: Which array method can remove or insert elements by mutating the original array?
questions.explanation: splice() changes the original array by removing, replacing, or inserting elements.

questions.text: What does the ternary operator use between the condition and the first result?
questions.explanation: The conditional operator has the form condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse.

questions.text: Which block handles an exception thrown inside try?
questions.explanation: A catch block handles exceptions thrown from the associated try block.

questions.text: A finally block can run whether the try block completes normally or throws.
questions.explanation: finally is designed for cleanup and normally runs after try and catch processing, regardless of success or failure.

questions.text: Which statement explicitly throws an exception?
questions.explanation: throw evaluates an expression and raises it as an exception.

questions.text: Which method converts a Set into an array using standard syntax?
questions.explanation: Array.from(set) creates an array from the Set's iterable values. Spread syntax such as [...set] also works.

questions.text: Which built-in collection stores unique values and preserves insertion order?
questions.explanation: Set stores unique values and iterates them in insertion order.

questions.text: A Map can use an object as a key.
questions.explanation: Map keys can be values of any type, including objects. Plain object property keys are limited to strings and symbols.

questions.text: What happens when a let binding is accessed before its declaration in the same scope?
questions.explanation: The binding exists in the temporal dead zone until its declaration is evaluated, so access before that point throws ReferenceError.

questions.text: Which statement about function declarations is generally true?
questions.explanation: Function declarations are instantiated before normal statement execution, so they are often callable before their source position.

questions.text: A class declaration can be safely accessed before the declaration line because classes are fully initialized during hoisting.
questions.explanation: Class declarations create bindings before execution but remain uninitialized until evaluation reaches the class declaration.

questions.text: How does Array.prototype.reduce() use its callback?

answers.text: To find only the first match

questions.explanation: reduce() repeatedly combines the accumulator with array elements to produce one final result.

questions.text: What equality algorithm does Set use for its values?
questions.explanation: Set uses SameValueZero. This treats NaN as equal to NaN and treats +0 and -0 as the same value.

questions.text: Which expression is true even though NaN === NaN is false?
questions.explanation: Object.is(NaN, NaN) is true. Strict and loose equality both treat NaN as unequal to itself.

questions.text: What is special about Object.is(+0, -0)?
questions.explanation: Object.is distinguishes +0 from -0, so Object.is(+0, -0) is false. Strict equality considers them equal.

questions.text: What does Function.prototype.bind() return?
questions.explanation: bind() creates a new function with a fixed this value and optionally pre-supplied arguments.

questions.text: Arrow functions can be used as constructors with new.
questions.explanation: Arrow functions do not have [[Construct]] and cannot be called with new.

questions.text: What does new.target indicate inside a function or constructor?

answers.text: Whether it was invoked with new

questions.explanation: new.target is defined for constructor-style calls and identifies the constructor that new invoked.

questions.text: Which statement about class methods is correct?
questions.explanation: Ordinary instance methods declared in a class body are defined on the class prototype and are non-enumerable.

questions.text: What does super.method() do in a derived class method?

answers.text: Calls a method on the parent prototype

questions.explanation: super.method() resolves the method from the superclass prototype while keeping the current receiver as this.

questions.text: What must a derived class constructor do before using this?
questions.explanation: A derived constructor must call super() before accessing this, because the base constructor initializes the instance.

questions.text: Private class fields declared with #name are accessible with bracket notation such as obj["#name"].
questions.explanation: Private fields use private names, not string property keys. They can only be accessed with # syntax where the private name is in scope.

questions.text: Which built-in language feature produces iterator values lazily with yield?
questions.explanation: Calling a generator function returns a generator object that implements the iterator protocol and yields values on demand.

questions.text: Which keyword yields a value from a generator function?
questions.explanation: yield pauses generator execution and produces a value to the iterator consumer.

questions.text: What does Symbol.iterator define for an object?
questions.explanation: A method stored at Symbol.iterator returns an iterator, allowing the object to participate in iteration protocols such as for...of.

questions.text: Which Promise combinator rejects as soon as any input Promise rejects?
questions.explanation: Promise.all() fulfills when all inputs fulfill, but rejects as soon as one input rejects.

questions.text: Which Promise combinator waits for every input to settle and never rejects because an input rejected?
questions.explanation: Promise.allSettled() waits for every input and fulfills with status objects describing each outcome.

questions.text: Promise.any() fulfills when the first input fulfills and rejects with AggregateError if every input rejects.
questions.explanation: Promise.any() ignores rejections until one fulfills. If none fulfills, it rejects with an AggregateError.

questions.text: Which Promise combinator settles with the first input that settles, whether fulfilled or rejected?
questions.explanation: Promise.race() adopts the outcome of the first input Promise to settle.

questions.text: When does a .then() handler run for an already fulfilled Promise?

answers.text: Immediately in the same call stack
Only on the next animation frame

questions.explanation: Promise reaction handlers are queued as jobs commonly exposed by browsers as microtasks, so they run after the current stack clears.

questions.text: Which browser API queues a callback directly in the microtask queue?
questions.explanation: queueMicrotask() schedules a callback as a microtask, which runs after the current task and before the next task.

questions.text: What does the delete operator do to a configurable own object property?
questions.explanation: delete removes a configurable property from an object. Assigning undefined leaves the property present.

questions.text: delete arr[1] reduces arr.length by one and shifts later elements left.
questions.explanation: delete removes the property but leaves a hole in the array. The array length does not shrink and later indexes are not shifted.

questions.text: Which Object.defineProperty() attribute controls whether a property appears in Object.keys()?
questions.explanation: Object.keys() includes own enumerable string-keyed properties, so the enumerable attribute controls inclusion.

questions.text: Which descriptor attribute controls whether a data property's value can be assigned?
questions.explanation: writable controls assignment to a data property. configurable controls deletion and most descriptor reconfiguration.

questions.text: What does Object.freeze() do to an ordinary object's own data properties?
questions.explanation: freeze() prevents extensions and makes existing own properties non-configurable; own data properties also become non-writable.

questions.text: Object.freeze() recursively freezes nested objects.
questions.explanation: Object.freeze() is shallow. Nested objects remain mutable unless they are separately frozen.

questions.text: What is true about ES module imported bindings?
questions.explanation: Imported names are live read-only views of the exporter's bindings, so later exporter updates can be observed.

questions.text: Which statement about top-level await is correct?

answers.text: It is allowed in ES modules

questions.explanation: Top-level await is valid in ES modules. It can delay dependent module evaluation without blocking the JavaScript thread.

questions.text: What does a Proxy handler's get trap intercept?
questions.explanation: The get trap intercepts property access operations on the Proxy.

questions.text: Why is Reflect.get() often useful inside a Proxy get trap?
questions.explanation: Reflect.get() performs the corresponding property get operation and can preserve receiver behavior when forwarding a trap.

questions.text: A Proxy handler may violate all target invariants without causing errors.
questions.explanation: Proxy traps must respect language invariants. Violating certain invariants causes a TypeError.

questions.text: Which collection allows object keys but does not keep those objects alive solely because they are keys?
questions.explanation: WeakMap holds keys weakly, so key membership alone does not keep an otherwise unreachable object alive.

questions.text: Which values may be WeakMap keys in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: WeakMap keys may be objects or non-registered symbols. Registered symbols and other primitives cannot be keys.

questions.text: What happens if a BigInt is mixed with a Number in arithmetic such as 1n + 1?
questions.explanation: Most arithmetic operators do not mix BigInt and Number operands, so 1n + 1 throws TypeError.

questions.text: Which operator can compare a BigInt and Number without requiring them to be the same type?
questions.explanation: Relational comparison can compare BigInt and Number values. Arithmetic mixing generally throws, and unary + does not support BigInt.

questions.text: What does structuredClone() provide for supported values?

answers.text: A deep clone using the structured clone algorithm

questions.explanation: structuredClone() deeply clones many built-in structured data types and can preserve cycles, unlike JSON serialization.

questions.text: structuredClone() can clone functions.
questions.explanation: Functions are not structured-cloneable, so attempting to clone one produces a DataCloneError.

questions.text: In const {x = 5} = obj, when is the default value 5 used?

answers.text: When x is null or undefined
Only when x is missing and null

questions.explanation: Destructuring defaults apply when the extracted value is undefined. A value of null, 0, false, or "" does not trigger the default.

questions.text: What does optional chaining obj?.method() do if obj is null?
questions.explanation: The optional chain short-circuits when obj is null or undefined, so the call is skipped and the expression yields undefined.

questions.text: Which statement about nullish coalescing is correct?
questions.explanation: ?? uses its right operand only when the left operand is null or undefined. Other falsy values are preserved.

questions.text: Which syntax creates a computed property name in an object literal?
questions.explanation: Square brackets in an object literal compute the property key from an expression.

questions.text: Which built-in symbol customizes how an object is tested by instanceof?
questions.explanation: A function-like object's Symbol.hasInstance method can customize the behavior of the instanceof operator.

questions.text: The right-hand side of instanceof can customize the check through Symbol.hasInstance.
questions.explanation: instanceof consults the right-hand side's @@hasInstance method when available, allowing custom instance checks.

questions.text: Which method changes a function call's this value and accepts arguments individually?
questions.explanation: call() invokes the function immediately with the supplied this value followed by individual arguments.

questions.text: Which method invokes a function with thisArg and an array-like list of arguments?
questions.explanation: apply() invokes the function immediately and accepts arguments from an array-like value.

questions.text: What does Object.create(proto) do?

answers.text: Creates an object with proto as its prototype

questions.explanation: Object.create(proto) creates a new object whose [[Prototype]] is the supplied value.

questions.text: Object.hasOwn(obj, key) checks only obj's own property, not an inherited property with the same key.
questions.explanation: Object.hasOwn() returns true only for an own property. The in operator, by contrast, also searches the prototype chain.

questions.text: Which comparison treats NaN as equal to itself and also distinguishes +0 from -0?
questions.explanation: Object.is() uses SameValue semantics: NaN equals itself, while +0 and -0 are distinct. SameValueZero does not distinguish the two zeros.

questions.text: What happens when an array's length is set to a smaller valid integer?

answers.text: Elements at removed indexes are deleted

questions.explanation: Reducing length deletes own array elements whose indexes are at or above the new length. Non-configurable elements can prevent full truncation.

questions.text: A destructuring default value is used when the matched value is null.
questions.explanation: Destructuring defaults are triggered by undefined, not null. null is treated as an explicit value.

questions.text: If queueMicrotask(a) runs before Promise.resolve().then(b) in the same task, which normally runs first?
questions.explanation: Both enqueue microtasks. With no intervening behavior, they run FIFO in the order they were queued, so a runs before b.

questions.text: What is required when a Proxy ownKeys trap reports keys for a non-extensible target?
questions.explanation: For a non-extensible target, ownKeys must report exactly the target's own property keys, subject to Proxy invariants.

questions.text: When does an iterator's return() method matter during for...of?
questions.explanation: IteratorClose can call return() when iteration ends abruptly or early, such as through break, allowing cleanup.

questions.text: How does Promise resolution handle a fulfilled value that is a thenable?
questions.explanation: Promise resolution adopts thenables by invoking their then method according to the Promise resolution procedure.

questions.text: Imported ES module bindings are writable from the importing module if the exporter used let.
questions.explanation: Imported bindings are live but read-only to the importer. The exporting module may update its own let binding.

questions.text: Which statement about Array.prototype.sort() in modern ECMAScript is correct?
questions.explanation: Modern ECMAScript requires a stable sort. sort() mutates the array, and without compareFn it compares string representations.

questions.text: What happens if Object.freeze() is called on a non-empty typed array with elements in current browsers?
questions.explanation: Freezing a typed array view with elements throws TypeError. A zero-length typed array can be frozen.
